olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Checkers on an $n\times n$ board: (a) every unchecked square shares a side with a checked one; (b) any two checked squares are connected by a sequence of checked squares sharing sides. Prove at least $(n^2-2)/3$ squares are checked.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1999

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $p>2$ be prime and $a,b,c,d$ integers not divisible by $p$ with $\{ra/p\}+\{rb/p\}+\{rc/p\}+\{rd/p\}=2$ for all $r\not\equiv 0\pmod{p}$. Prove at least two of $a+b,a+c,a+d,b+c,b+d,c+d$ are divisible by $p$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1999

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ ($n>3$) be real with $\sum a_i\geq n$ and $\sum a_i^2\geq n^2$. Prove $\max a_i\geq 2$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1999

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: The Y2K game on $1\times 2000$: players alternate writing S or O. First to spell SOS wins; if full without SOS it's a draw. Prove the second player has a winning strategy.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1999

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Isosceles trapezoid $ABCD$ with $AB\parallel CD$. Incircle of $\triangle BCD$ touches $CD$ at $E$. $F$ on the angle bisector of $\angle DAC$ with $EF\perp CD$. Circumcircle of $\triangle ACF$ meets line $CD$ again at $G$. Prove $\triangle AFG$ is isosceles.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1999
